label: copy-phase input g fed back as the 1st or 2nd copied token
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, when the fed-back input token is g at the first two copy-phase inputs (recall_idx 1 or 2, so the g being fed back is original token 0 or 1). Magnitude is strongly modulated by position: it is strongest (about 0.85-1.0 of max) when g is the first original token, fed back right after <DEL> (recall_idx 1). This case holds about 82% of activation mass and every such step is active. When g is original token 1, fed back at recall_idx 2, it fires weakly (about 0.1-0.35 of max). It is essentially silent on g during the original phase, on g fed back later in the copy (recall_idx >= 3), and on every other token. Output token and sequence length have little effect.

issues: The core claims hold. All activation mass is in the copy phase, in_tok g carries 100% of it, and recall_idx 1 holds 81.6% of the mass with recall_idx 2 holding 18.4%. On dev, recall_idx 1 with g has precision 1.0. Test scores reproduce: P 0.968, R 0.997, F1 0.982.

Systematic false-positive class: g at recall_idx 2 depends on sequence length, which contradicts the explanation's claim that length has little effect. Dev precision of (phase==2)&(in_tok==g)&(recall_idx==2) is 0.097 at L=3 (464 predicted), 0.716 at L=4 (2362 predicted), 0.9985 at L=5 and 1.0 at L=6. Test misses show the same thing: almost all of the 1058 false positives are short sequences such as 'n g k <DEL> n *g*' and 'm g z 1 <DEL> m *g* z'.
At L=4 the feature does fire on g at recall_idx 2 when orig(0) is also g (precision 1.0 on 82 steps), so whether it fires at L=4 partly depends on history.
Missed activations (102 steps on test, 0.0% of mass) are tiny values of about 0.01-0.04 on g at recall_idx 3, which is scattered noise.
The gap is small (about 1-3% of predictions), so the feature is still explained. The fix is to exclude L=3 at recall_idx 2: test F1 rises to 0.988 and precision to 0.980.
